node.name: package-lock.json
node.rich_text:
## What is `package-lock.json`?
It's an **exact snapshot** of every package installed in `node_modules` — including the precise version, download URL, and checksum of every single dependency.
---
### Difference between `package.json` and `package-lock.json`:
| File | Purpose | Example | |---|---|---| | `package.json` | Your wishlist — "I want React ~19" | `"react": "19.2.4"` | | `package-lock.json` | Exact record — "I installed React 19.2.4 from this exact URL with this exact hash" | Full tree locked |
---
### Simple analogy:
``` package.json = shopping list ("buy milk") package-lock.json = receipt ("bought Lola milk 1L, from Store X, batch #ABC123, paid $1.20") ```
---
### Why it exists:
Without it, two developers running `npm install` on different days might get **different versions**:
``` Developer A installs on Monday → react-dom 19.2.4 ✅ works Developer B installs on Friday → react-dom 19.2.5 ❌ breaks
With package-lock.json: Both get EXACTLY 19.2.4 ✅ always consistent ```
---
### Key facts:
| Fact | Detail | |---|---| | **Auto-generated?** | Yes — by `npm install` automatically | | **Edit it?** | Never — npm manages it | | **Commit to GitHub?** | Yes ✅ — always commit it | | **Size** | Can be thousands of lines | | **Recreate it?** | `rm package-lock.json && npm install` |
---
### It's already in your project:
``` frontend/package-lock.json ← committed to GitHub ✅ frontend/package.json ← committed to GitHub ✅ frontend/node_modules/ ← NOT committed (in .gitignore) ✅ ```
---
### Summary:
``` package.json = "what packages I need" (you write this) package-lock.json = "exact versions installed" (npm writes this) node_modules/ = "the actual packages" (npm downloads this) ```
Always commit `package-lock.json` — it guarantees everyone on the team gets identical packages.
